summary.headline: Minda Corp Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 2,189 crore, up 43% YoY, with PAT of INR 143 crore up 69%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a record quarter: revenue INR 2,189 crore (+43% YoY, +19% QoQ), EBITDA INR 257 crore (11.8% margin) and PAT INR 143 crore (6.5% margin). Management attributed the strength to EV products, new TFT and sunroof programmes and the consolidation of Minda VAST. Margins were pressured by commodity and input costs, minimum wage revisions and higher freight, though management said input cost increases are largely pass-through with a one-quarter lag. H1 FY27 normalised PAT was INR 243 crore, excluding a INR 106 crore one-time gain from the Minda VAST consolidation in Q1. Management also announced a greenfield TFT display module plant under the ECMS scheme.

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: About 31% of Q2 revenue. About 10% of wiring harness revenue is from EV platforms; high-voltage cables for the top-selling Indian passenger vehicle are 100% localised.

segments.name: Vehicle access systems
segments.commentary: About 24% of Q2 revenue, with the increase attributed to consolidation of Minda VAST (JV with WITTE, Germany).

segments.name: Die casting, clusters and others
segments.commentary: About 15% of Q2 revenue (about INR 330 crore). Growth driven by EV mobility products (chargers, power electronics), sensors, antennas, wireless chargers, interior plastics and motors; management cited EV parts and electronics as the highest traction.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Europe and North America about 6% of revenue, South Asia about 5%, India about 89%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects input-cost increases (commodities, copper) to be recovered from customers with about a one-quarter lag under back-to-back indexation.
Share of renewable power targeted at 80% to 90% by 2035; currently about 30% to 35%. A new solar power arrangement is expected to save INR 2 to 3 per unit.
Expected revenue mix over the next couple of years: two- and three-wheelers 40% to 45%, commercial vehicles 20% to 25%, passenger vehicles 25%+.
Management referred to a Vision 2030 target and said it has delivered on promises over the last five quarters. It disputed an analyst's reference to 30% CAGR guidance.
capex_capacity: Greenfield TFT display module assembly plant in Chakan/Pune region via 100% subsidiary Minda Instruments, approved under ECMS; investment about INR 200 crore in phases; SOP about 18 months out; asset turnover expected at 3x to 4x.
Target to localise 70% to 80% of TFT display requirements, which are currently fully imported.
About 6 to 7 new plants under construction, commencing operations in 12 to 24 months; these include instrument cluster, TFT display, switches, die casting, wiring harness and EV product plants.
Existing base of 42 manufacturing plants and about 23,000 employees; land bank about 8.2 lakh sq m with about 2.6 lakh sq m built-up.
Dedicated high-voltage wiring harness facility in north India for passenger vehicles.
demand_pricing: Management cited industry growth in Q2: two-wheelers about 16.5%, passenger vehicles about 25%, three-wheelers about 24%, commercial vehicles about 34%; Minda's revenue growth of 43% was described as well ahead of about 18% industry growth.

New orders: TFT instrument cluster orders (5 to 12 inch) with cumulative lifetime value above INR 1,000 crore across 2W, 3W, CV and PV, production from FY28. A 3.5 kW charger order from a 3W OEM, production in Q1 FY28. EV products were about 35% of new order wins in the quarter and about 35% of order book value.
Sunroof production started this quarter (panoramic sunroof content about INR 20,000 per vehicle); first power footstep order from an anchor PV customer.
Typical SOP timing: starts about 18 to 24 months after order receipt, with peak about 2 years later. About 50% to 60% of business comes from new platforms.
Margin pressures in Q2: elevated commodity prices, input costs, minimum wage revisions across several states and higher freight. Management declined to share TFT or sunroof margins.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is needed for the display module entry, what is the timeline, and what is the TFT integration potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment of about INR 200 crore in phases, SOP in about 18 months, asset turnover of 3x to 4x, and localisation of 70% to 80% of TFT requirements.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the growth in the other products segment?
qa_highlights.answer: EV mobility products (chargers, power electronics), sensors, antennas, wireless chargers, interior plastics and motors. EV parts and electronics show the highest traction.

qa_highlights.question: How much copper inflation is in wiring harness revenue, and will there be more price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Copper price increase is about 4% to 5% of the wiring harness business. It is back-to-back indexed with customers with a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix of renewables in power and the expected savings from the solar deal?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% to 35% of power is currently renewable; target is 80% to 90% by 2035; savings expected at INR 2 to 3 per unit.

qa_highlights.question: Which revenue segments will become significant over the next 2 to 3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Passenger vehicles are expected to move to 25%+ of revenue from 18% to 20% now; two- and three-wheelers 40% to 45%; commercial vehicles 20% to 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the instrument cluster split by vehicle segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 40% two-wheeler, 30% commercial vehicle and 30% passenger vehicle.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q2 EBITDA margin of 11.8% was hit by commodity, wage and freight costs, and recovery from customers lags by one quarter.
Execution risk on the INR 200 crore TFT plant and the 6 to 7 plants due in 12 to 24 months.
Management did not disclose TFT or sunroof margins, and declined to give EV revenue share targets in numbers.
Q2 PAT of INR 143 crore includes a Q1 one-time gain effect in H1 figures; H1 reported PAT of INR 243 crore excludes the INR 106 crore gain and is shown as normalised.
Dependence on imported TFT displays until the new plant is commissioned (about 18 months).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order wins and the record quarter; more guarded on margins, with cost pressures described as pass-through. Management declined to give margin and EV revenue numbers for new products, and pushed back on the 30% CAGR framing by pointing to Vision 2030.
key_quotes: Minda Corporation delivered a landmark quarter, achieving strong performance across revenue, EBITDA and profit.
So this will be the range or the speed, I would say, we are going to further penetrate into the products.
Our stated principle is that by 2035, 80% to 90% of our power should come from renewable energy.
I think we have already shared our Vision 2030 and not 30% CAGR just to correct you.

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue guidance; growth backed partly by specific orders (TFT cluster orders with >INR 1,000 crore lifetime value from FY28, 3.5 kW charger order for Q1 FY28) and capacity coming live over 12-24 months (6-7 plants, TFT plant ~18 months SOP), but no overall FY guidance number given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 11.8% (H1 11.6%) was pressured by commodity, minimum wage and freight costs; recovery from customers lags one quarter, and TFT and sunroof margins were not disclosed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 6 to 7 new plants are under construction with operations due in 12 to 24 months, and the INR 200 crore TFT module plant has an SOP about 18 months out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 43% YoY versus about 18% industry growth, EV products were about 35% of new order wins, and TFT cluster orders above INR 1,000 crore lifetime value start from FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The INR 200 crore greenfield TFT module plant under ECMS is approved and phased, and a dedicated north India high-voltage harness facility is planned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric revenue or margin guidance was given for the year, so an upgrade cannot be assessed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margins were hit by commodity, wage and freight costs and customer pass-through lags one quarter, so a margin miss is possible even though management says costs are pass-through.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A 3.5 kW charger order is due for production in Q1 FY28, TFT cluster production starts in FY28, and sunroof and power footstep programmes are already ramping.

rows.label: TFT instrument cluster orders above INR 1,000 crore lifetime value
rows.why: Cumulative lifetime value above INR 1,000 crore across 2W, 3W, CV and PV is already won, with production starting in FY28.

rows.label: Back-to-back copper and commodity indexation
rows.why: Copper inflation of about 4% to 5% of wiring harness revenue is passed to customers with a one-quarter lag, which should recover cost in the following quarter.

rows.label: Renewable power share and solar savings
rows.why: Renewable share is about 30% to 35% against an 80% to 90% target by 2035, and the new solar deal saves INR 2 to 3 per unit, but there is no near-term timing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record quarter, EV and TFT order wins and capacity coming online, but guarded on margins and declined to disclose TFT or sunroof margins; analysts pushed on the 30% CAGR framing and margin pass-through, which management answered by pointing to Vision 2030.
